# Independent audit: sampled-superlevel hyperplane concentration

Audited `candidate a779c844eb8df3e4` in full and
reran `supporting computation verify_sampled_superlevel_hyperplane_concentration.py` with
plain Python. **PASS; no correction needed.** The numerical-seed
loop in the verifier evaluates rational certificates exactly; the
general theorem follows from the written argument, not that loop.

The triangulation can include every boundary and interior lattice
point by stellar subdivision of its minimal face. It remains pure
and its full-simplex dual graph is connected: a path in the convex
polytope interior can avoid codimension-two faces and cross facets
transversely. A spanning-tree traversal starts with r+1 vertices
and introduces at most one per further simplex. Thus t>=|A|-r.
Lattice determinants give volume at least v/r! per simplex. Both
constants in vol(conv A)>=(|A|-r)v/r! are correct.

The greedy selection uses r affinely independent points. Every
point outside the FINAL hyperplane was eligible at every earlier
stage, so all selected values are at least the outside maximum b.
For every 0<t<b, the strict superlevel contains the selected r
points and one point outside their hyperplane, hence has full rank.
The proof never applies the full-rank bound to higher superlevels,
which may be lower dimensional and carry arbitrarily large sampled
mass. Layer-cake gives exactly sum min(f(p),b)-rb; the r selected
points pay rb, every outside point pays its full value, and the
remaining terms are nonnegative. Ties cause no endpoint loss.

If the positive sampled support is rank deficient, its rational
affine span lies in a lattice hyperplane. A nonzero integral
annihilator of its difference span constructs this plane; it can
be spanned by r affinely independent lattice-coset points. This
handles the zero-integral and lower-dimensional-superlevel cases.

For convex-body sections, boundedness and upper semicontinuity
follow by taking Hausdorff limits of bounded sections and using
their inclusion in the limiting section. Brunn--Minkowski gives
convex strict positive superlevels. The counting case s=0 correctly
uses an indicator, not a zero root. A unimodular simplex times a
positive s-body attains the outside mass r!M/v exactly, proving
sharpness including all-positive sampled fibers.

The retained-source construction includes each ENTIRE original
positive fiber on the selected hyperplane. Its hull stays in the
original convex body. Any additional integer base in its projected
hull has positive s-volume by a positive full-dimensional summand
in its Minkowski representation, so it was already among those
included fibers. Thus all retained lattice fibers are exact. A
saturated relative lattice basis changes only base coordinates,
preserving H_s volumes and every containing ambient halfspace
restriction. The selected lower-rank center is an actual original
point, including when some restrictions are the whole relative
ambient space.

Finally the normalized factors in (5)--(6) are correct. Averaging
the retained masses over at most J levels loses precisely 1/J,
and reducing one fine integer dimension gains the factor two in
the conditional OC budget. The condition M/(vT)<=1/(2r!) supplies
half the total fine mass and yields the stated target when J<=2^k.
No allocation across unbounded J is implied. For r=1 only the
ordinary continuous Grunbaum theorem is used.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
